correctness.rationale: Monomial norms yield q=1/m-1/(m+tau(m!)^2) in [0,1/m). For m>=4 the real part has lower bound 1-log 2-1/m>0; for m=3 boundary cos(3theta) split and harmonic minimum principle imply strict positivity; for m=1 convexity in q between extremal boundary-positive kernels does likewise. For m=2 the imaginary sign formula Im F/y=integral_0^1|1-ut|^{-2}du-2qx>0 (Jensen and |t|<1) excludes nonreal zeros; positive t is nonzero; G_q(r)=1-log(1+r)-q r^2 strictly decreases and crosses zero in (0,1) iff q>1-log2. The boundary case tau=tau_* does not give an interior zero. Checks: 18 boundary samples, 3 negative roots and independent analytic comparisons, not inference from samples.

value.rationale: A natural finite-rank RKHS norm perturbation has a surprisingly isolated zero-producing jet order and an exact sharp Lu Qi-Keng transition. The zero-freeness boundary of this explicit Dirichlet family is reusable in analytic kernel and interpolation questions, not merely a renamed textbook bound.

final_claim: For the coefficient-normalized analytic Dirichlet space, adding one central m-jet penalty gives scalar kernel 1-log(1-t)-q t^m. Exactly m=2 admits interior zeros; its threshold is tau_*=(1-log 2)/(2 log 2-1). Above the threshold there is one simple negative-real scalar zero; at equality the root is only on excluded boundary t=-1.
